findings.issue: The ARCHITECTURE.md §5 'date earlier than the last issued number' watermark is evaluated exactly once, before the retry loop (the MaxAsync over OfficialNumbers.LastDate at line ~186). It is never re-evaluated after a lost race. Interleaving: context B reads the watermark (say 2026-09-10) and is about to issue for 2026-09-10; context A commits a number dated 2026-09-11; B's SaveChanges loses the concurrency check (or the PRIMARY KEY race), B reloads the row (LastDate now 2026-09-11), then unconditionally executes `row.LastDate = today` with today = 2026-09-10 and commits. The result is an official number whose date is earlier than an already-issued number of the same kind, and official_numbers.last_date regresses — the very invariant the pre-loop check exists to enforce, silently bypassed on exactly the path this package hardened. Same-day contention (the common case) is unaffected, which is why no test catches it.
findings.fix: Re-check the watermark inside the retry loop rather than only before it. After the `row` is obtained/reloaded at the top of each iteration and before `row.LastSeq += 1`, add: `if (today < row.LastDate.Date) { throw new InvalidOperationException("official numbering refused: date is earlier than the last issued number"); }` (keeping the existing cross-year MaxAsync pre-check for the case where this kind has no row for `year` yet). Add a test that seeds a committed row with LastDate = 2026-09-11 on one DbSession, pins a second DbSession's tracked row at the older date/seq exactly as Issue_WhenAnotherContextIssuedInBetween_IsRetried_AndTheNumbersDiffer does, then asserts the retry refuses instead of writing back the earlier date.

SPEC ITEM 1 (INSERT race) — CLOSED, genuinely. IssueCoreAsync now catches DbUpdateException (the base type, so DbUpdateConcurrencyException is covered by the same catch) filtered by IsSequenceRaceException, which requires BOTH (a) exception.Entries.Any(e => ReferenceEquals(e.Entity, row)) and (b) either the exception is a DbUpdateConcurrencyException or the inner SqliteException carries SqliteErrorCode 19 AND SqliteExtendedErrorCode 1555/2067. That is correct and materially narrower than the raw `SqliteErrorCode == 19` the round-1 fix suggested: code 19 is also NOT NULL/FOREIGN KEY/CHECK, and IssueAsync's own SaveChangesAsync flushes every other change the caller has tracked on the same context. OfficialNumber's key is the composite HasKey(Kind, Year) (WakeelDb.cs:461), so the losing insert really does surface as extended code 1555, and LastSeq.IsConcurrencyToken() (WakeelDb.cs:467) covers the UPDATE race. Tests: Issue_WhenAnotherContextInsertedTheVeryFirstRowFirst_IsRetried_AndTheNumbersDiffer (two DbSessions over the same file, winner 1 / loser 2, numbers differ), Issue_WhenAnotherTrackedEntityViolatesAnUnrelatedConstraint_PropagatesTheOriginalException_NotMisreadAsARace, Issue_WhenRetriesAreExhausted_ThrowsOfficialNumberConcurrencyException_PreservingTheSqliteException, and the new Issue_WhenTheConflictingRowVanishesBeforeTheReload_DetachesTheStaleAddedEntry_AndTheRetrySucceeds.

SECURITY / CONCURRENCY REVIEW. EnsureInTransaction() guards both public overloads before any read or write, and Issue_WithoutAnOpenTransaction_IsRefused_OnBothOverloads asserts nothing was written to official_numbers or clock_checks. Uniqueness under concurrency holds on both axes: the composite PK blocks a duplicate first row and IsConcurrencyToken blocks a stale increment, so the only way to commit sequence N is to have observed N-1 in the row EF matched. The retry loop re-queries at the top of every iteration, so LastSeq, the MaxSequence exhaustion check and the number string are all recomputed from refreshed state — no stale sequence can be handed out after a retry. The retry is bounded (5, overridable only through an internal test-only constructor gated by InternalsVisibleTo) and exhaustion surfaces as the dedicated OfficialNumberConcurrencyException with the original DbUpdateException preserved as InnerException, so a caller's IErrorMapper mints exactly one reference. The one gap I found is the un-rechecked date watermark, filed as the single low finding above; it does not let two callers receive the same number, only an out-of-order date under cross-date contention.

DELIBERATE DEVIATION (not a finding). Round-1's suggested fix said to let the final attempt's exception "be mapped by ErrorMapper". The builder instead introduced OfficialNumberConcurrencyException and documented the reasoning at length on both the interface remarks and the exception type: mapping inside the service would mint a reference nothing logs and a second, different one when the caller maps the escaping exception, and would be indistinguishable from the InvalidOperationExceptions this service throws for user-actionable business refusals. I agree with that call — it satisfies the intent of the finding (nothing escapes as a raw DbUpdateException) and is strictly better for the error-reference contract. No user-facing string was added; every message on this path is an English programming/infrastructure message the user never sees, and the Arabic user-facing refusals are unchanged.
